l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time ACARS & ACMS flight alerts
l4_steps.input: Continuous ACARS datalink messages, ACMS fault codes, crew SELCAL calls
l4_steps.output: Confirmed irregularity event record in NOC operations log
l4_steps.kpi: Alert acknowledgement within 2 minutes of ACARS receipt; 100% alert capture rate
l4_steps.pain_point: High ACARS message volume creates noise; controllers must distinguish genuine emergencies from routine fault codes without cockpit confirmation — risk of delayed response during shift handover

l4_steps.name: Classify emergency type and severity level
l4_steps.input: ACARS alert, pilot voice report via Telex/SITA ACARS or VHF relay, flight plan data
l4_steps.output: Emergency classification (Medical / Mechanical / Weather / Security / Other) and severity (Level 1–3) logged in OCC system
l4_steps.kpi: Classification completed within 5 minutes of initial alert; misclassification rate <1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Ambiguous early reports from cockpit force controllers to act on incomplete information; multi-type events (e.g. medical + mechanical) may be misclassified, delaying correct response track

l4_steps.name: Determine if full emergency declaration is required
l4_steps.input: Emergency classification, aircraft type performance limits, crew request
l4_steps.output: Go / No-Go decision for emergency declaration; Emergency Response Plan activation trigger
l4_steps.kpi: Decision latency <3 minutes from classification; 0 missed full-emergency escalations
l4_steps.pain_point: Ambiguity in Level 2 events where crew has not declared Mayday/Pan-Pan; NOC may under-declare to avoid costly ARFF standby fees, creating liability exposure if situation worsens

l4_steps.name: Identify candidate diversion airports and performance data
l4_steps.input: Aircraft current position, fuel state, emergency type, weather METARs/TAFs
l4_steps.output: Ranked list of suitable alternate airports with runway performance calculations and estimated fuel on arrival
l4_steps.kpi: Alternate identification completed within 5 minutes; fuel calculation accuracy ±50 kg
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time runway contamination and NOTAM status not always reflected immediately in NAVBLUE; stale NOTAMs risk selecting an airport with active runway closure

l4_steps.name: Evaluate diversion airport suitability and slot availability
l4_steps.input: Candidate airport list, aircraft MTOW, runway length/PCN data, weather forecasts, slot constraints
l4_steps.output: Approved diversion airport with confirmed runway compatibility, available ground services, and weather minima
l4_steps.kpi: Evaluation complete within 4 minutes; 100% runway compatibility verified before recommendation
l4_steps.pain_point: Coordinated airports (Level 3) require slot approval that cannot be obtained in real-time during emergency — dispatcher must accept non-compliance risk and coordinate retroactively with slot coordinator

l4_steps.name: Confirm diversion decision and alternate airport selection
l4_steps.input: Dispatcher recommendation, fuel state, medical urgency (if applicable), crew preference
l4_steps.output: Confirmed diversion instruction logged in OCC; crew notified via ACARS and voice
l4_steps.kpi: Diversion instruction transmitted to crew within 10 minutes of initial alert; 0 diversions to airports with insufficient runway performance
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew and NOC may disagree on preferred alternate; without clear authority hierarchy in SOPs this creates delay — particularly when crew has elected an airport not on the approved alternate list

l4_steps.name: Coordinate ATC diversion clearance via datalink
l4_steps.input: Confirmed diversion airport, squawk code (7700/7600/7500), current ATC sector
l4_steps.output: ATC diversion clearance received; amended flight plan filed; OOOI update transmitted
l4_steps.kpi: ATC clearance obtained within 3 minutes of diversion decision; 100% amended flight plan filed within 5 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: In non-radar oceanic airspace or remote FIRs, HF voice communication is required instead of datalink — significantly increasing coordination time and controller workload

l4_steps.name: Activate Emergency Response Plan and notify ERT
l4_steps.input: Confirmed emergency declaration, incident classification, ERP checklist
l4_steps.output: Emergency Response Team assembled; checklist activated; notification log initiated
l4_steps.kpi: ERP activation within 5 minutes of emergency declaration; 100% of required ERT contacts notified within 10 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: ERP contact trees rely on manual phone call cascades — if primary contacts are unavailable during off-hours, escalation path is unclear and notification time degrades significantly

l4_steps.name: Alert ARFF, medical, and emergency services at diversion airport
l4_steps.input: Confirmed diversion airport, flight number, aircraft type, number of passengers, nature of emergency
l4_steps.output: ARFF category confirmed; medical standby ordered; airport operations alerted; AMS event record created
l4_steps.kpi: Diversion airport notified within 5 minutes of diversion decision; ARFF on standby confirmed ≥15 minutes before estimated landing
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS interface with some regional airports is limited to telex-only — automated notification fails and NOC must resort to direct phone calls, introducing manual error and delay

l4_steps.name: Determine if hospital transfer or specialist medical support needed
l4_steps.input: Cabin crew medical report via ACARS, MedLink or equivalent in-flight medical advisory service output
l4_steps.output: EMS / ambulance request confirmed or waived; hospital pre-notification triggered if required
l4_steps.kpi: Medical severity determination within 5 minutes of crew report; EMS request placed ≥20 minutes before landing for Level 1 medical events
l4_steps.pain_point: In-flight medical advisories (e.g. MedLink) are contracted by airline but cabin crew may not initiate contact in time; late escalation reduces hospital preparation time and increases patient risk

l4_steps.name: Notify regulatory authorities per emergency event type
l4_steps.input: Emergency type, squawk code used, aircraft registration, event timeline
l4_steps.output: FAA ATC notification confirmed; NTSB/AAIB preliminary notification filed if required; airline safety officer looped in
l4_steps.kpi: Regulatory notification completed within 30 minutes of event; 100% compliance with ICAO Annex 13 / FAR Part 830 reporting timelines
l4_steps.pain_point: International diversions trigger multi-authority notification requirements (local CAA, ICAO state of registry, ICAO state of operator) — manual tracking in OCC frequently results in missed or delayed filings

l4_steps.name: Reserve gate, parking, and coordinate ground handling at diversion airport
l4_steps.input: Aircraft type, estimated arrival time, passenger count, special handling requirements
l4_steps.output: Gate or remote stand assigned; ground handling agent notified; fuel order placed if required; PRM assistance requested
l4_steps.kpi: Ground handling confirmation received ≥20 minutes before estimated landing; 100% PRM passengers pre-identified and notified to handler
l4_steps.pain_point: At outstations with no contracted ground handler, NOC must arrange ad-hoc handling at premium cost with unpredictable service levels — especially critical for widebody or heavy aircraft at small airports

l4_steps.name: Arrange immediate passenger care and amenity provision
l4_steps.input: Passenger manifest, diversion airport facilities, estimated delay duration, special needs passengers flagged
l4_steps.output: Passenger care plan activated (meals, accommodation vouchers, transport); unaccompanied minor and MEDA passengers prioritised
l4_steps.kpi: Passenger care plan communicated to diversion station within 30 minutes of landing; vouchers issued within 1 hour per EC261/DOT consumer protection requirements
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS does not automatically flag all MEDA passengers to diversion station — manual cross-check of Special Services Requests is required, creating risk of missed care for vulnerable passengers

l4_steps.name: Assess whether passengers can continue on diverted aircraft
l4_steps.input: Aircraft technical status, crew remaining duty time, fuel state, ATC slot availability, estimated delay
l4_steps.output: Go / No-Go decision to continue flight on same aircraft; if No-Go, recovery plan initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Continue / cancel decision communicated to passengers within 45 minutes of landing; 0 illegal crew departures approved
l4_steps.pain_point: Pressure from station managers and passengers to resume quickly can bias NOC toward premature Go decision before maintenance and crew legality checks are complete

l4_steps.name: Rebook affected passengers on next available services
l4_steps.input: Passenger manifest, destination, next available flight inventory, interline agreements
l4_steps.output: Rebooking confirmations issued; PNR updated; boarding passes reissued; IROPS waiver applied
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of affected passengers rebooked within 2 hours of diversion landing; involuntary reroute documented for EU261/DOT compensation tracking
l4_steps.pain_point: Disrupted inventory during IROPS means preferred rebooking flights are often sold out; interline rebooking on partner carriers requires manual ticketing if NDC agreements are not in place

l4_steps.name: Verify crew duty time legality for continued or return operations
l4_steps.input: Crew sign-on times, actual block hours flown, rest requirements under FAR Part 117 / EASA FTL
l4_steps.output: Crew legality assessment report; approved continuation or rest requirement logged
l4_steps.kpi: Legality check completed within 30 minutes of diversion landing; 0 regulatory FTL violations incurred
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen Crew Management may not have real-time position updates for diverted crew if ACARS OOOI data is delayed — manual reconciliation required, increasing error risk under time pressure

l4_steps.name: Source and position relief crew if original crew is illegal
l4_steps.input: Crew illegality flag, diversion airport location, reserve crew availability, positioning options
l4_steps.output: Relief crew identified and travel confirmed; estimated time to diversion airport logged in OCC
l4_steps.kpi: Relief crew identified within 1 hour of illegality determination; positioning confirmed within 2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve crew availability at outstations is typically zero — positioning from base requires commercial travel or ferry flight, leading to delays of 4–12 hours and potential AOG at diversion airport

l4_steps.name: Assess aircraft airworthiness and coordinate maintenance release
l4_steps.input: ACMS fault data, MEL/CDL checks, maintenance release requirements at diversion airport
l4_steps.output: Aircraft serviceability determination; maintenance work order raised if defect found; Return-to-Service sign-off or AOG declared
l4_steps.kpi: Initial airworthiness assessment within 60 minutes of landing; AMOS work order raised within 15 minutes of defect confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Diversion airports rarely have the airline's contracted MRO present — sourcing an approved Part 145 maintenance organisation at short notice is costly and time-consuming, frequently resulting in AOG delays exceeding 24 hours

l4_steps.name: Submit incident report and complete post-event regulatory filings
l4_steps.input: Full event timeline, ATC comms log, crew statements, maintenance findings, passenger impact data
l4_steps.output: Internal incident report filed; mandatory regulatory reports submitted (FAA MOR, ASIAS, ICAO occurrence report); lessons-learned triggered
l4_steps.kpi: Internal report completed within 24 hours; FAA Mandatory Occurrence Report filed within 72 hours per FAR Part 830; 100% of required attachments included
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-event reporting relies on manual assembly of data from multiple systems (ACARS logs, AMS, Jeppesen, AMOS) with no automated aggregation — data gaps and inconsistencies frequently require follow-up with multiple departments, delaying final filing
